value.text:
One look at Scary Jerry and you understood the name.

Jason Macleone was imposing before he ever threw a pass, and then he threw 9,970 of them. He completed 67 percent for 73,799 yards and 771 touchdowns, with just 128 interceptions across 331 games. He took 86 sacks and never lost a fumble. When he did tuck it and run, he made it count: 71 rushing touchdowns.

His defining day came in Y78, when he quarterbacked the Vikings past the Broncos 33-27 in Super Bowl CXXXVII. Two rings, three MVPs and a Super Bowl MVP in all, and he finished his career in Seattle, where every start added to the case.

The league's line of great quarterbacks runs from Lamar through Gooden, Waller, Baylon, Brandson and the Wilson brothers. It runs through him. Scary Jerry, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Eleven tackles a game, every game, for 236 games.

Abraham Ward Jr played in the Green Bay secondary, and his stat line reads like a linebacker's. He made 2,653 tackles and picked off 33 passes along the way. He was never credited with a sack or a forced fumble. He did not rush the passer and he did not strip the ball. He found the ball carrier and put him on the ground, snap after snap, season after season.

The Packers made him a champion in Y79, when they beat the Chiefs 44-6 in Super Bowl CXXXVIII, and the league named him Defensive Player of the Year. One ring and one award can look like a small haul for a career this long. The tackles tell the rest of the story.

He crossed into the Hall in Y82 and kept adding to the total until he retired. Abraham Ward Jr, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Few linemen have ever been busier on a snap-for-snap basis than Jawill Perkins.

He played 139 games and was credited with 304 blocks, a shade under two and a quarter every time he lined up. Among the league's linemen only Calais Ham blocked at a higher rate. He never piled up the games of the iron men up front. He made the games he played count.

He has four rings to show for it, without a single MVP or Player of the Year award, because that is how the position works. The credit goes to the quarterback who stays clean and the back who finds the lane. Perkins is the reason the lane was there. Seattle wears him on its banner.

Four rings, 304 blocks, and one of the best rates the position has seen. Jawill Perkins, welcome to the Hall of Fame.
